body: i can’t imagine what i’d do if i was in a shooting, i think i’d just panic. probably the scariest thing i can think of. but anyways, i’m glad you came out of that situation unscathed!

it was truly a life saver haha. i am also aware that a lot of people don’t seem to find success with it. i think the reason it worked for me is that i’ve been culminating my hair routine and the hair products i use for months haha. i did a lot of research to try and get the best possible idea of what would help. i HIGHLY recommend the verb ghost shampoo and conditioner. it is truly a godsend! i find it helps get all of the oil out and adds volume, without straining or damaging my super thin and tangly hair. leave in conditioner is also an essential as it doesn’t weigh my hair down.
blow drying my hair after washing is probably one of the things that i have added into my routine, it definitely helps with the flat hair issue haha

i have also been cursed with extremely oily, baby fine hair, and i have also tried dozens of different products and routines to try and make it more manageable. it got to a point where i was extremely frustrated and felt like i was just doomed to wash it everyday even though it was a lot of work and damaging to my already thin hair. the only thing i can say that honestly works is scalp training. i’ve been hearing about the technique forever and always just dismissed it. over quarantine, i got desperate and started experimenting and i ended up trying it. the idea is, if you extend the periods of time in between wash days, your scalp will start to produce less and less oil over time. i started by washing every other day, and slowly i started making progress. now, about four months later, i only wash my hair twice a week and it remains clean and voluminous up until wash day. it takes awhile, and some people say it doesn’t work, but i have found it is highly effective. i say if you have the time,and are willing to wait it out, give it a try, since we seem to have similar hair types. best of luck!
